title: 'He's made it clear': Wayne Gretzky backs PM Carney's call to bar Russia from world juniors
summary: Wayne Gretzky says he backs Canada's decision to bar Russia from the upcoming world junior hockey championship in Alberta.

blocks.text: Wayne Gretzky says he backs Canada's decision to bar Russia from the upcoming world junior hockey championship in Alberta.
'I think a lot of the players and the people of Canada feel the same way,' says hockey icon
Prime Minister Mark Carney said earlier this week Russian and Belarusian athletes will not be permitted to represent their countries on Canadian soil while the war in Ukraine continues.

The decision came after the Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled Russia must be reinstated to international hockey competition, starting with the world juniors. Russian and Belarusian teams have been banned since Moscow's 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

blocks.text: Speaking at a Friday ceremony hosted by Upper Deck to rename the Hockey Hall of Fame's resource centre in honour of his late father, Gretzky said he understands the position Carney has taken.
Carney says Russia won't be allowed to play in upcoming world juniors
The Great One praised Carney for making his position clear, saying "good for him" before adding, "I think a lot of the players and the people of Canada feel the same way."
The world juniors are scheduled to run from Dec. 26 through Jan. 5 in Edmonton and Red Deer.
